security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU uses any of the following stale SPMP behavior: (1) siselect/miselect decode maps SPMP entries via ordinal indices 0..63 instead of the new hex base 0x100..0x13F, causing indirect SPMP CSR access to read/write wrong registers or fall into unmapped CSR space; (2) accessing SPMP CSRs while SPMP is disabled (pmpnum == total_entries, zero entries delegated) raises an illegal-instruction trap instead of silently returning zero on reads and ignoring writes, breaking guest software that probes or tolerates disabled SPMP; (3) pmpnum WARL coercion prevents M-mode from incrementing pmpnum past a locked SPMP entry index, when the spec now explicitly allows pmpnum to override locked SPMP entries (only locked PMP entries block pmpnum reduction); (4) S-mode write to siselect targeting a locked SPMP entry toggles the L bit instead of being silently ignored, allowing S-mode to unlock its own entries
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: siselect decode table for indirect SPMP CSR access, miselect decode table for indirect SPMP CSR access, spmp_disabled gate raising RISCV_EXCP_ILLEGAL_INST, pmpnum WARL coercion treating locked SPMP same as locked PMP, siselect write handler clearing L bit on locked entries
security_spec.summary: PR#72 rc4→rc5: siselect/miselect select values re-encoded from ordinal to hex base 0x100; disabled-SPMP trap replaced with silent zero/ignore; pmpnum must override locked SPMP entries; S-mode can no longer lock SPMP entries; SFENCE.VMA ordering clause relocated and clarified — QEMU CSR decode, trap routing, WARL coercion, and lock-bit enforcement must all be updated
